question: Which of the following protocols is commonly used for data encapsulation in WANs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**High-Level Data Link Control**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• High-Level Data Link Control (HDLC) is a protocol used for data encapsulation in Wide Area Networks (WANs).

• HDLC is a bit-oriented protocol for communication over point-to-point and multipoint links.

• It provides both connection-oriented and connectionless services.

• HDLC is known for its reliability and efficiency in data transmission over long distances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Wide Area Network (WAN)**

• A WAN is a telecommunications network that extends over a large geographic area for the primary purpose of computer networking.

• WANs are used to connect smaller networks, such as local area networks (LANs) or metro area networks (MANs).

• They enable devices from different locations to communicate as if they were part of the same local network.

• **Wi-Fi**

• Wi-Fi is a wireless networking technology that uses radio waves to provide high-speed Internet and network connections.

• It is commonly used for local area networking of devices and Internet access.

• Wi-Fi is not typically used for WANs but for home and office networks.

• **Ethernet**

• Ethernet is a family of networking technologies commonly used in local area networks (LAN), metropolitan area networks (MAN), and wide area networks (WAN).

• It is a wired communication technology that provides network connectivity over physical cables.

• Ethernet is primarily used for short-distance communication within a single building or campus.

• **TCP/IP**

• TCP/IP stands for Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol.

• It is a set of communication protocols used to interconnect network devices on the Internet.

• TCP/IP specifies how data should be packetized, addressed, transmitted, routed, and received.

• It is the foundation of Internet communication.
